authorization: Pedro, 2026-09-12, in as many words: 'eu aprovo explicitamente a religaçao do hash e a mudança no atuador'. He had already retracted, the same day, the standing refusal to lengthen a contact in the view region ('um toque prolongado dentro da regiao nao faz pan, isso e um mau entendido de quando nao sabiamos sobre o desync de estado de mascara/monitor'), which is what reopened this knob. He also asked, before this binding, whether the change degrades Nights 6 and 7; it does not.
scope: fifth binding of the same measured hid-mediaprojection transport -- UHID game input via /system/bin/hid, MediaProjection visual observation via Cue Helper, one bounded device-local HID schedule per night with abort-on-gameover and releaseAll -- re-bound to the minus-toys story Night 5 winner with every press moved clear of the compiler's device timing floors (tools/device/campaign-toys-night5-winner.json, winnerHash fnv1a-2fc303f1, bundle replay fnv1a-924edf66, night-5 plan sha256 8155f1d7cf4699c44ace7b6754756cdcc4cfe894e33ad6e36a0d7aca73096445, profile hid-mediaprojection sha256 c929d673a056b4d7ef1839bccc4666986e2a1991b39232c0869046b0d68ae6e0)
planDelta: Two contact lengths and one compensation: loopContactMs 33 -> 200 (already bound and run: 37/37 clean, 372.5 s), camdropMonitorMs 33 -> 200, and openMaskLeadMs 349 -> 182 so the longer camdrop contact does not move the opening's mask tap (+4482 either way; emitted opening bytes identical). hallMs stays 33 -- see openLimits.
whyItMoved: camdropMonitorMs was the only loop contact still at 33 ms, which equals FUSION_POLL_MS, and the peer audit of the contact200a frame trace traced ALL THREE of that run's second-attempt corrections to it being swallowed (toys-6 MISSING at +14000, +144000, +164000 at both ends of the clock bracket, each followed by a BUTTON ABSENT mask press under a still-raised monitor). Zero 200 ms presses were lost in the same trace.
bounds: Swept all seven nights, normal and worst, 3000 seeds: 3000/3000 everywhere. The model cannot show the benefit -- it does not simulate a swallowed tap -- so this is ABSENCE OF HARM. The benefit is the device measurement of the previous binding.

evidence.claim: the binding this supersedes; same transport, four floor knobs
the mask window tolerates [-200, +175] ms of position, so a corrected cycle arriving 800-950 ms late is dead regardless -- the loss has to be prevented, not corrected

openLimits: hallMs stays 33 and is REFUSED, not deferred: the model gives night 1 worst 0/3000 above 67 ms and night 2 worst 0/100 at 200 ms, two different ceilings, and no hall tap has been proven lost

the 200 ms mask-off contact makes the hall flash LESS often (peer census: 40% dark at 33 ms, 58-61% at 200), and the hall tap at +9500 clears the post-mask flash lockout by only ~56 ms against MASK_ANIM_OFF ~244 ms; hallOffsetMs is the knob that addresses this and is unswept here
the 372.5 s death on the previous binding was NOT a swallowed contact and has no cause label; Foxy is the hypothesis the hall census points at, not a finding

openMaskLeadMs 182 is a compensation for an emitter derivation that anchors the opening mask on the camdrop's END while the compiler and the game both anchor monitor-down at the PRESS; the coupling should be removed at the derivation rather than carried as a knob
